title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: production traffic shows occasional long-tail latency spikes when the continuous batcher prioritizes large requests and long sequences, causing smaller/short-lived requests to be starved. This PR tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler to improve queueing fairness, introduce request aging, and add explicit starvation timeouts so latency SLOs are preserved. Motivation: reduce p99 tail latency for interactive workloads without regressing overall throughput or per-token cost. Changes include a new per-request priority decay (aging) policy, a configurable starvation timeout with a fallback fast-path, improved queue admission checks to avoid head-of-line blocking by oversized batches, and better instrumentation for debugging scheduling decisions. The description below outlines the approach, tests, and operational guidance. Approach: 1) Priority decay: each enqueued request now accumulates an "age_score" that decays the effective weight of long-running high-cost requests and increases priority of older queued requests; this prevents a stream of large requests from permanently outranking small, latency-sensitive ones. 2) Starvation timeout: requests include a configurable starvation_deadline_ms; once exceeded the scheduler either forces the request into the next batch (fast-path) or triggers a lightweight preemption of a candidate request to make room. 3) Batch admission heuristics: tighten admission checks to consider both current in-flight KV cache pressure and expected token runtime, preventing oversized batches from blocking progress. 4) Observability: new metrics (batcher.queue_age_p90, batcher.preemptions, batcher.starvation_timeouts) and tracing tags describing why a request was delayed/forced. 5) Config: new runtime flags: continuous_batcher.priority_decay_half_life_ms, continuous_batcher.starvation_deadline_ms, continuous_batcher.enable_preemption (boolean), and admission.max_effective_batch_cost. Tests & validation: unit tests for priority decay math, integration tests simulating mixed small/large workloads, a perf harness that reproduces the previous tail-case and shows p99 tail latency improvement (~25%) with <3% throughput regression. CI: added flaky-tolerant integration tests and an optional perf job that runs on the perf lab. Rollout plan: roll out feature behind a runtime-safe flag, enable on Canary pool, monitor batcher.* metrics and p99 latency, then gradually increase traffic if stable. Operational notes: default starvation_deadline_ms set to 200ms for interactive routes (overrides permitted per route); preemption is off by default and only enabled if safe for model and KV cache semantics. Migration notes: changes are backward-compatible at the API level; internal scheduler behavior changes only. Related: ENG-2981, ENG-3110; incident INT-5412 recorded the original tail issue.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Can we avoid preemption for requests that depend on large KV cache warmups? Concerned about model cold-start correctness.
Aisha Patel: Good point, added a KV cache safety check; preemption will skip requests flagged as 'kv_warmup_required'.
Sofia Mehta: The priority decay math looks reasonable but we should document the half-life default and how it affects short vs long sequences.
Aisha Patel: Added docs and defaults.yaml entry; half_life default set to 150ms with examples in observability doc.
Ethan Zhang: Unit tests are flaky on arm builders due to timing granularity. Can we use simulated clocks for tests?
Aisha Patel: Switched integration tests to simulate clocks and added a fallback timing tolerance for wall-clock tests.
Sofia Mehta: Approving after KV safeties and simulated-clock changes.
